reviewer.role: independent bounded CODE configuration-kernel implementation-prompt reviewer

scope: Read-only review of the implementation prompt against the accepted CODE-CONFIG-KERNEL R1 contract, R2 clarifications, CODE-PROOF-CLOSURE R3, the accepted R2 static fixture, and the preparation acceptance. No production source, test source, fixture, Git, network, connector, Vault, dispatch, or extra-agent mutation.
verdict: The prompt is bounded and dispatchable after the separately required Git-kernel acceptance and CODE-CONFIG-KERNEL-freeze-r1.json. It carries the R1 API and safety boundary, incorporates both R2 semantic closures, binds the accepted static fixture by provenance and hash requirement, names exactly three prospective source paths, and requires the necessary fixture, supplementary-vector, boundary, callback, cross-check, determinism, and dual-runtime checks. No semantic contradiction or implementation-scope blocker was found. The remaining gate is procedural: the freeze must bind the exact successor source root/head/tree, final allowlist, fixture bytes/hash, and required input hashes before dispatch.

dispatch_prerequisites: Architect acceptance and local delivery of the Git kernel
CODE-CONFIG-KERNEL-freeze-r1.json created and explicitly named by dispatch
freeze-bound exact source root, accepted baseline head/tree, allowlist, fixture and input hashes
execution_policy: Grok Build CLI grok-4.6 / xhigh only
no Git mutation, external acquisition, dependency/model installation, real Vault/admin operation or unrelated source access
refuse source-root or baseline mismatch and never fall back to the outer repository

allowed_paths_check.fixture_rule: The fixture path is required to be a byte-exact copy of accepted static-vectors-r2.json; regeneration, repair, legacy edits and unrelated source/schema/test/metadata changes are prohibited.
allowed_paths_check.brief_rule: The separate freeze names the sole new development-brief path; the future brief must record contract/freeze/session/model/effort, changed paths, commands/results, failures or unrun checks, all three path hashes/sizes, and source_writes_stopped=true.

checks.evidence: The prompt delegates the pure API to CODE-CONFIG-KERNEL-R1 plus unchanged R2 clarifications and keeps CODE-PROOF-CLOSURE-R3 as the numeric/source-coordinate authority. It forbids I/O, imports of supplied source, dynamic evaluation, subprocesses and global Decimal/integer-limit changes.

It requires scanner limits and exact source-coordinate representation before the independent whole-tree json/tomllib cross-check, and prohibits unbounded stdlib parsing or regex-only source searching.

checks.area: strict types, key safety and owned state
checks.evidence: It carries the exact-builtin-dict and constant-time-length guard, exact builtin str verification before callback-triggering operations, callback traps for non-exact primitives/keys, and owned primitive limit snapshots.

It names original byte/codepoint spans, decoded-key identity, TOML table states, finite numeric semantics, all thirteen limits, declaration-before-insertion accounting, deterministic ordering, no aliasing, and no partial node list on refusal.

The prompt requires dynamic offset vectors and supplementary groups while preserving the R2 token-start rule and exact error behavior through its unchanged-clarifications input; it also requires escaped keys/newlines, Unicode positions and marker/callable cases.

The 26-vector transition matrix is explicitly normative supplementary input rather than a source whitelist, and tests must exercise promotion, dotted prefixes, closed inline boundaries and duplicate semantics.

Tests must assert fixture source and every expected_nodes record, derive budget expectations independently, treat extra notes as provenance, and run every success/refusal vector plus both supplementary groups.

The prompt requires numeric/string/depth/node/declaration boundaries, CRLF/multibyte/escaped/surrogate/span cases, hostile Decimal contexts, parser mismatch for changed types/keys/order/values, cross-check corruption, and no traceback leakage.

It requires span and text/snippet hash comparison with pure legacy test helpers, complete focused-module runs on locked Python 3.12 and 3.13, the locked environment variables, and short real /private/tmp directories.
